name: esbuild
summary: A fast JavaScript and CSS build system that parses source files into typed representations, resolves an import graph, and links reachable modules into bundled or transformed outputs.

features.name: Typed source AST representation
features.description: The fixed source exposes JavaScript AST and import-record structures, and its parser returns an AST for a source file. The representation carries syntax, symbols, imports, exports, and source metadata into later build stages.
benefits: Separates parsing from resolution and output generation
Carries source-level structure into optimization and linking
costs: AST and import metadata consume memory for large graphs
Language-specific syntax and lowering rules increase parser complexity

features.name: Parallel module graph scanning
features.description: The fixed bundler source implements ScanBundle as a graph-scanning phase, adds entry points, parses discovered files, and uses concurrent work while resolving reachable imports. The graph records input files, entry points, and import relationships before linking.
benefits: Makes independent file parsing and resolution work concurrent
Provides a reusable reachable-module graph for output decisions
costs: Concurrency requires synchronization and deterministic result handling
Graph construction scales memory with reachable inputs and import records

features.name: Linker and output boundary
features.description: After scanning, the fixed bundler invokes a linker over reachable files and entry points. The linker is the boundary where module relationships, code splitting, and output serialization are turned into generated files, while the API exposes bundling and transformation as distinct operations.
benefits: Keeps graph discovery separate from output-specific serialization
Supports multiple entry points and output grouping
costs: Output format and code-splitting choices constrain graph transformations
Generated output must preserve module semantics across target environments

features.name: Incremental rebuild state
features.description: The official API documents a context API for retaining build state across rebuilds and watch operations. This gives repeated builds a persistent context rather than requiring every request to recreate all build configuration and graph state.
benefits: Supports watch and repeated rebuild workflows
Allows retained build state to amortize setup work
costs: Retained state requires explicit disposal and lifecycle ownership
Invalidation rules must keep changed inputs consistent with cached state

mathematical_views.question: How do parsed source modules and import records define the reachable graph from one or more entry points?
assumptions: Modules are vertices and resolved imports are directed edges
Parser and resolver implementation details are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: Which transformations map source text through parsing, graph scanning, linking, and generated output?
assumptions: Each phase consumes a typed intermediate representation
The scan phase establishes reachable inputs before linking
Output serialization and target lowering are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: What retained build state can be reused when an input or build request changes?
assumptions: A context represents retained state across rebuild requests
Changed inputs induce a bounded invalidation relation
The public API does not by itself prove the exact invalidation algorithm

benefits: Structured parsing enables later graph and output phases
costs: Intermediate representations add memory and language-specific complexity

benefits: Independent graph work can proceed concurrently
costs: Synchronization and graph memory become build-system concerns

benefits: One graph can feed target-specific output strategies
costs: Linking must preserve semantics while applying output constraints

benefits: Repeated builds can reuse retained context
costs: Lifecycle and invalidation correctness become caller-visible obligations
